_ruling: owner live 2026-10-08 session 1 (pack 0.35.1, first session after a reset): every point where the owner had to ask back is a defect. A lift with no measured basis gets its load from CODE: a labelled estimate at entry, a first set classified by e1RM (calibration rung vs working set 1), and a concrete next weight after every set. live_load.py is the one reader of this file.

band._why: the target band is the slot rep_range [lo, hi]; a one-number range is widened by the tolerance so a set one rep off is not a calibration. The RIR the band is measured at is the HIGH end of the slot's target-RIR band (rx-calc resolve_target_rir), the same reserve e1rm_rx_rules.json backsolve.rir uses; rir_default only when the slot has no band.

calibration._rung_why: owner 2026-10-10 12:47-12:50: a warm-up rung reported without RIR is read at the warm-up reserve (4), never at RIR 0 -- an e1RM with no RIR assumes failure and stepped 60x5 down to 50. A FIRST set short of the band with no RIR on a calibrating lift is a rung too (no step-down on reps alone): it is stored in the ramp lane and the RIR is asked. A coach-armed target is never at or below a WARM-UP rung completed today (no RIR, or 4+; live_load.ramp_target / above_rungs) -- a rung with a stated RIR under 4 is a measurement and its e1RM decides (live batch 2 probe rule). Only an owner-named weight is a ceiling for rungs while the lift calibrates.
calibration._margin_why: a first set is a ramp-up only when its implied reps clear the band top by MORE than this: 26kg x10 @RIR3 on 8-10 (implied 11) is a slightly light working set, 50kg x15 @RIR4 on 5-8 (implied 17) was a warm-up.
calibration._why: first working set on a lift with no measured basis (no rx weight, no prior-session working set): implied = reps + rir - rir_target. ABOVE hi -> it was a ramp-up: a calibration rung (warm-up), stored in the ramp lane, and the next set is re-prescribed from its e1RM. Inside -> working set 1. BELOW lo stays working set 1: that set was the owner's real effort, and live batch 2 item 1 (set-arm calibration_step_down) steps the next set down from it. With no RIR reported the implied count is a lower bound, so only a set that is ABOVE the band even then is a calibration. And only when the grid offers a better weight: a light stack whose next pin is already past the band (5kg x 15 @RIR2 on 12-15, next pin 7.5) re-prescribes the same number, so that set is working set 1.

next._why: the next weight is the grid point (the confirmed machine's pins incl. a known add-on block, else the slot lattice, else the default increment) whose implied reps at the target RIR land in the band, closest to the band middle; none in band -> the point closest to the band; ties -> the lighter. Implied reps use the pack's one e1RM formula (e1rm_rx.set_e1rm).

estimate._why: a lift with no measured basis gets a LABELLED estimate at entry: target e1RM = anchor e1RM (bench-equivalent for upper, squat-equivalent for lower; today's session first, else the newest session that logged the anchor) x ratio x conservative, back-solved at the rep_range bottom with the band-high RIR (the rx backsolve rule) and snapped DOWN on the grid. Ratios are e1RM ratios keyed by exercise_movement_grip movement/equipment; dumbbell ratios are per hand. No anchor -> no estimate (never a minimum-pin fallback; accessory-weight.md).
